title: Delta eval for prefetch KV cache consistency and rollout safety
creator: Liam O'Rourke
description:
Objective:
Build and operationalize a deterministic delta-evaluation harness and rollout guard for the prefetch/kv prefix cache so that any cache hit (or change to cache policy/config) that materially changes model outputs is flagged, scored, and gated from automated rollouts. This ticket covers the test harness design, metrics/threshold definitions, alerting integration, and an automated canary blocking rule that can be used by the rollout service.

Background:
We observed occasional output divergences when serving model variants with different cache prefetch/eviction policies and with quantized kernels. Existing datasets (ENG-4720, ENG-12458) detect broad drift but do not provide a fast, per-config safety signal suitable for CI and canary rollouts. The goal here is a lightweight, reproducible delta test that runs as part of model/config rollout pipelines and the nightly regression job.

Scope and deliverables:
- A harness that replays a curated set of ~2k prompts (golden set + synthetic stress cases) through the exact same model weights and runtime but with cache enabled vs disabled (or alternate cache policies) and records token stream diffs and semantic deltas.
- Two comparison layers: (1) token-level deterministic diffs (edit distance, first-token divergence point), (2) semantic similarity via sentence-embedding cosine + normalized logit delta on top-k.
- Scoring rubric that combines: divergence ratio, mean semantic cosine drop, and a heuristic for meaningfulness (e.g., change in intent classification or instruction-following failures).
- Thresholds for blocking automated canary rollouts + a 'severity' score used by the Console to create a regression incident.
- Integration with CI (GitHub actions) and the rollout service: a job that runs the delta eval on model/config change PRs and returns pass/fail; and a nightly job that re-evaluates release candidates.
- Dashboard and alerting: a lightweight dashboard on Grafana (links below) and PagerDuty alerts for severity >= high.

Design decisions & notes:
- We intentionally separate token-level and semantic checks to catch both tiny but semantically severe changes and higher-level drifts that token diffs miss.
- The harness will use a deterministic RNG/seeded KV cache warmup sequence to minimize nondeterminism. When nondeterminism occurs, we log the seed and environmental metadata to reproduce locally.
- For performance, the primary CI run will sample 200 prompts (fast path) and the nightly/PR full run uses 2k prompts (thorough path).
- We will parameterize the test to run across these config deltas: cache_enabled=true/false, prefetch_window=[0,32,128], eviction_policy=[LRU, FIFO], kv_quantization=[none, int8], batching_window_ms=[0,10,50].
- False positive mitigation: the scoring rubric requires both an absolute semantic delta threshold and a relative change in top-3 token probabilities. This reduces spurious blocks from innocuous paraphrases.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike (2 days): implement minimal harness that runs X prompts locally and computes token/semantic diffs. Deliverable: python CLI + small dataset.
2) Expand to CI hook & parameter sweep (3 days): GitHub Actions job template + configuration matrix for cache params.
3) Integrate with rollout service (2 days): provide an API that returns {pass, fail, severity, report_url}. Add blocking rule to canary pipeline.
4) Dashboard & Alerts (2 days): Grafana dashboard + PagerDuty playbook for severity >= high.
5) Documentation & runbook (1 day): Confluence doc and troubleshooting steps.

Artifacts / links:
- Spike branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2978 (WIP)
- Golden prompt set (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/cache-delta/goldset-2025-11
- Draft PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CACHE/Delta+Eval+for+KV+Prefetch+Cache
- Grafana dashboard (dev cluster): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-delta/kv-cache-delta (provisioned)
- Rollout rule spec: https://go.redwood.ai/rollout-rules#kv-delta-block

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can produce a deterministic report comparing cache on vs off for the sample set and a severity metric for the change.
- CI job exists and is invoked on PRs that change any cache-config or kernel selection code.
- Canary rollout blocks automatically when severity >= medium (configurable) and posts a formatted regression report link to the rollout activity log.
- Dashboard surfaces daily counts of regressions and top offending prompts/config combos.

Risks and mitigations:
- Non-deterministic LLM outputs: mitigate via seeding, identical runtime config, and repeated runs to detect flaky inputs.
- High false positive rate: use combined token+semantic rubric and conservative blocking thresholds for first rollout (only alert on medium+, block on high).
- Performance impact to CI: sample-based fast-path reduces PR latency; full dataset runs nightly.

Next steps (short term):
- Spike complete and PR created (ENG-branch). Need review from runtime and evals team on metric choices.
- Schedule 1-hour sync with Console/rollout owners to agree on severity-to-action mapping (blocking vs alerting).
